summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of necrotizing soft tissue infection, psoriatic arthritis, morbid obesity, and recent pulmonary embolism was admitted from a rehabilitation facility due to worsening left leg pain, redness, and drainage. He was found to have cellulitis with elevated white blood cell count and was started on intravenous vancomycin and Zosyn. The infectious process resolved with treatment, and antibiotics were discontinued after clinical improvement. He remained on heparin infusion due to subtherapeutic INR despite high-dose warfarin, with plans to continue anticoagulation at the rehabilitation facility. A new PICC line was placed during admission due to infection concerns, and a lower extremity Doppler ruled out deep vein thrombosis. He was discharged in stable condition with follow-up arranged in acute care, hematology, and infectious disease.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Secondary diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, uncontrolled
Personal history of Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus
Adrenal cortical steroids causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
